summary: RDP module speaks the X.224 CR handshake, parses RDP Negotiation Response for security-mode / NLA posture (T1), and does an extra TLS+CredSSP TSRequest to harvest an NTLM CHALLENGE + CredSSP version (T1 info + version-based CVE claim). BlueKeep detection is candidate-only (banner-fingerprint) not confirmed. Doesn't ever attempt authentication - per user directive T3 stays as tester_next_step. Gap: no BlueKeep safe verify (there's a known non-destructive MS_T120 channel probe).

findings.title_pattern: RDP: Network Level Authentication (NLA) not required
findings.tier_evidence: Server accepted selectedProtocol=0 (STANDARD_RDP) - direct wire observation NLA is not required. Deterministic, non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: Add rdesktop-style credential prompt MitM demonstration (proves the plaintext capture path) - stays T2 without hitting the actual target. Or wire a safe BlueKeep verify (MS_T120 channel-close race probe from nmap smb-vuln-cve-2019-0708 variant - benign check).
findings.tester_next_step: xfreerdp /v:<ip>:<port> /sec:rdp - confirms Standard RDP; nmap -p <port> --script rdp-vuln-ms12-020,rdp-enum-encryption <ip>; if Win7/2008R2: nmap --script rdp-vuln-cve-2019-0708 (safe check, does NOT trigger BSOD).

findings.tier_evidence: Just prints negotiated protocol / nla_required / standard_rdp_accepted - pure fingerprint, always emitted.
findings.promotion_notes: Baseline info; escalation belongs in the other kinds (no_nla, ntlm_info, credssp_unpatched).

findings.title_pattern: RDP CredSSP NTLM CHALLENGE leaks host/domain intel
findings.tier_evidence: One extra TLS+CredSSP TSRequest carrying NTLMSSP Type-1 parses the returned Type-2 for AV_PAIRs (NetBIOS/DNS/AD domain/forest/OS build) - deterministic pre-auth harvest via MS-CSSP 3.1.5.
findings.promotion_notes: Info-disclosure ceiling reached. Cross-service value is feeding known_hostnames/known_domains - ensure the analyze() folds ntlm_info into host.ntlm the way winrm does (currently it just stores on the target dict).
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -p <port> --script rdp-ntlm-info <ip>; then feed dns_domain into kerberos + os_version into CVE search.

findings.title_pattern: RDP CredSSP is unpatched for CVE-2018-0886
findings.tier_evidence: TSRequest version <=2 read directly from server's TSRequest reply - version <=2 IS the pre-March-2018 patch level per MS advisory. Deterministic version-based CVE claim.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 would require an actual MitM demonstration with a controlled logon credential injection payload - complex, hard to do safely. Stays T1 unless a canary-driven MitM harness lands.
findings.tester_next_step: Metasploit auxiliary/scanner/rdp/cve_2019_0708_bluekeep (safe check) - but for CVE-2018-0886 exploitation requires MitM position and controlled credentials; not typically exploited on internal without additional access.
